title: Subarray Sum Equals K
statement: Return how many contiguous, non-empty subarrays of the list add up exactly to k. Values may be negative or zero.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(7)
    return [[r.randint(-5, 5) for _ in range(100000)], 0]

hints.1_question: A subarray sum is a difference of two prefix sums. If prefix[j] - prefix[i] == k, what must prefix[i] be?
hints.2_nudge: As you scan, keep a map of how many times each prefix sum has occurred. How many earlier prefixes equal (current - k)?
hints.3_big_hint: seen = {0: 1} (empty prefix). For each x: total += x; count += seen.get(total - k, 0); seen[total] += 1.

known_bugs.name: forgets the empty prefix (seen starts empty)
known_bugs.followup: How does your code count a subarray that starts at index 0? What prefix sum corresponds to 'before the first element'?

known_bugs.name: sliding window (breaks with negatives)
known_bugs.followup: Sliding windows rely on the sum only growing when you extend. Is that true if the array can contain negatives or zeros?

known_bugs.name: set instead of counts (undercounts repeated prefixes)
known_bugs.followup: If the same prefix sum appears three times, how many subarrays can end here? Does a set remember that?

followups: Why can't a sliding window solve this when negatives are allowed?
How would you return the subarrays themselves instead of the count?
